Ms. ___ is an ___ year old female with a history of Stage I

T1bN0M0 invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR+  
and HER2- of the R breast diagnosed in ___ s/p modified 
right mastectomy (no adjuvant hormone therapy) who presents with 
worsening low back pain and left lower extremity paresthesias.

She called her PCP ___ asked her to go tho the ED 
for expedited evaluation.
She had been in her USOH until early
___ when she began to have left hip and low back pain.

Her left lower extremity paresthesias involving the left lateral 
calf began two to three weeks ago and occur only when she 
stands.

She has not noticed weakness; however, three days prior 
to admission she sustained a fall while walking down the steps 
of her home.
This had never happened to her in the past.

There 
was no LOC or headstrike, lightheadedness, sz activity or trip.
She thinks she fell because of her excruciating pain.

She broke 
the fall with her hands and sustained a laceration to the right 
arm which required several sutures.

I have not seen her outside records which are being located now; 
however, a detailed desciption of her studies done in the last 
two weeks is provided in the radiaton oncology note from 
tonight: "MRI of the L-spine was ordered and  
performed on ___ that revealed a marrow replacing lesion  
involving the posterior left side of the L3 vertebral body  
involving the left pedicle and left superior and inferior 
facets.
Linear T2 hyperintensity involving the superior aspect of the L3
vertebral body reflected associated fracture.

The report notes  
that these findingsweare highly suspicious for metastatic 
disease  
given the patient's history of breast cancer and tissue sampling
was advised.
Dr. ___ a bone scan performed on

___ which revealed a poorly defined left L3 osteolucent  
lesion in the vertebral body pedicle and left transverse process

with increased activity in upper L3 extending into the left  
transverse process, possibly consistent with an infiltrating  
process causing pathologic fracture as there was mild L3 upper  
endplate collapse new since ___ plain films and ___ CT.
There was punctate increased uptake in the R side of T2, T3, or

T4 without radiographic correlate, and increased indeterminate  
activity in R anterior 4th rib near costochondral junction,  
possibly posttraumatic or marrow infiltrating lesion.

Plain 
films  
of ___ on ___ revealed several mild wedge compression  
fractures at T6-T8 with no lytic or sclerotic lesions.

Plain  
films of L-spine on ___ revealed mild probably pathologic  
fracture of upper L3 with lytic lesion of left L3 pedicle and  
transverse process."

In the ED, initial VS were T98.4, HR 81, BP 163/90, RR 18, O2 
sat 100%.
Exam did not show any focal neurological deficits.
Labs were unremarkable.

Ortho spine evaluated her for cord 
compression, and they felt this was unlikely based on a clinical 
exam.

Apparently she had a CD with her imaging but it has not 
been loaded into the system and we are trying to locate it.

She 
was also seen by radiation oncology, who felt she should be 
admitted to medicine for expedited work up and pain control.

She 
was given dilaudid .5mg iv, lorazepam .5 mg iv, and 1LNS.

VS 
upon transfer were T98.4, p 67, 147/80, r 18, 99% RA.
Currently

She continuted to complain of severe worsening pain in back, L 
groin, L hip, L leg.

Also having numbness/tingling and 
subjective weakness in L leg x 2.5 weeks.
No incontinence.

No 
fevers but occasional chills. 5 lbs weight loss in 2 weeks.
Unable to perform ADLs d/t pain.

Also had a fall earlier this 
week and left wrist is now in a splint, but reportedly no 
fracture.
ROS:

+ chills, abdominal pain, occasional nausea associated with her 
pain, constipation,weight loss, weakness, shortness of breath

- fever, night sweats, headache, vision changes, rhinorrhea,

IMPRESSION:

1. Extensive metastatic replacement of the L3 vertebral body and 
its left posterior elements, with some retropulsion of its 
dorsal cortex.

There is an associated left epidural and 
foraminal soft tissue component narrowing the left subarticular 
zone, likely impinging upon the traversing left L4 and, 
possibly, more caudal nerve roots at that site, as well as the 
exiting left L3 nerve root in that foramen.

2. Slight anterior wedge deformities of the T7 and T8 vertebrae, 
likely chronic, with no evidence of acute pathologic vertebral 
compression.
3. Additional metastatic foci in the T6, likely T8, T9, T12 and
L2 vertebrae, without associated soft tissue abnormality.
4. No pathologic leptomeningeal or radicular enhancement.

5. Degenerative disease at the C4-5 and C5-6 levels, with 
significant spinal canal narrowing and ventral cord remodeling, 
incompletely imaged.

6. Evidence of extensive periventricular white matter 
abnormality, which may represent sequelae of chronic small 
vessel ischemic disease, incompletely imaged.
___ Radiology CT L-SPINE W/O CONTRAST

Lytic, expansile lesion involving the left L3 vertebral body 
extending through the pedicle into the posterior elements.

Soft 
tissue encroaches on the spinal canal, though this is better 
evaluated on the MRI of the same date.Abnormal soft tissue is 
also seen within the left neural foramina at L2/L3 and 3/L4.

There is mild compression deformity at L3; however, no fracture 
ragments enter the spinal canal.

___ yo F with Stage I T1bN0M0 invasive ductal carcinoma, ER/PR+ 
and HER2- of the R breast diagnosed in ___ s/p modified 
right mastectomy (no adjuvant hormone therapy) who presents with 
progressive low back pain, left lower extremity paresthesias, 
left hip pain in the setting of a reportedly new lytic lesion in 
the posterior left side of the L3 vertebral body and wedge 
compression fractures in T6 to T8 of unknown chronicity.
ACTIVE ISSUES BY PROBLEM

# L3 lytic lesion: highly concerning for malignant metastasis, 
with breast cancer the likely primary.

MRI showed lesion in L3 
and also likely metastatic foci throughout numerous vertebrae in 
the thoracic spine as well.

No evidence of cord compression or 
cauda equina.

Pain in L hip/leg likely from impingement of L3-4 
nerve roots causing radicular, neuropathic pain.

Ortho spine 
evaluated her imaging (also had lumbar CT) and felt that her 
spine was stable but recommended a brace for further stability 
and pain control.
She was started on standing tylenol, tramadol

(oxycodone made her "groggy", lidocaine patch, and gabapentin 
for pain relief.

Radiation oncology evaluated the patient and 
felt that radiation therapy could be helpful in relieving pain 
from the impingement, but they recommended biopsy for definitive 
tissue diagnosis prior to any radiation plans.
(she prefers to be treated near home) for tissue diagnosis.

She was educated on the 
warning signs for cord compression and cauda equina and told to 
go to the ED immediately if she develops any of those symptoms.
CHRONIC, INACTIVE ISSUES:

# Menopausal Syndrome:  her estrogen replacement was held due to 
the possibility of relapsed breast cancer
# GERD and Esophagitis: continued omeprazole
# HTN:  continued lisinopril, amlodipine
# Depression:  continued citalopram
# Allergic asthma: continued albuterol inh prn and montekulast
